title: Zac Taylor Recaps Win over Miami | PRESS CONFERENCE
headline: Tee Higgins played through a questionable tag, Ja'Marr Chase cleared protocol, and Joe Burrow's thumb jam is minor; the Bengals now get a bye before at Baltimore.
summary: Taylor credited Miami for fighting to the end and praised Jeff Hafley's work with the Dolphins. He listed the Bengals' issues: two personal fouls, two red-zone fumbles, a kickoff caught on the four, a field-goal penalty that led to a touchdown, and over 200 rushing yards allowed. He said the bye arrives at a good time after three straight close games, and the team will regroup at 3-2 before Baltimore in two weeks. He said the defense's late turnover made the final margin feel safer. On the run game, he said the ground success was mostly how the game unfolded, with Miami playing underneath and in shells, and he called the team's backs a strength he trusts. He downplayed Burrow's hand injury as a jammed thumb on his non-throwing hand. He said Tee Higgins had wanted to play and showed it in practice, and that Ja'Marr Chase had cleared concussion protocol on Saturday. He praised Tanner Hudson as dependable and versatile, able to play multiple spots, and said he needed the defense to settle on its nickel and base personnel. He called the heat historically extreme and said the players fought through exhaustion.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/11/26
headline: Quinn takes full blame for the end-of-game clock decision in a tie, while Jayden Daniels returned from missed time and played sharply.
summary: Quinn called the game a hard-fought tie that felt like a loss. He said the late-game decision to run for more yards instead of clocking the ball or throwing it out was his responsibility, not Daniels'. He said the team had the chance to win in all three phases and did not seize it, and he praised Daniels' overtime forced fumble on defense. On Daniels, Quinn said it was great to have him back, and he highlighted his line-of-scrimmage reads against blitzes, his willingness to use his legs without forcing it, and his accurate throws to Terry McLaurin and Treylon Burks in crunch time. On defense, Quinn said the unit needs to close out games and shut the door when leading, and that the team is digging in on its response after second-half collapses. He said the penalties, especially pre-snap ones, are being addressed but that he has not yet reviewed the Amik Robertson pass interference call at the goal line. He acknowledged injuries in the secondary and at receiver, and said the team handled the depth challenge well. He said the team will rebound, and that the end-of-game situation will be drilled more heavily in practice.

injuries.detail: Returned after missing time and played the full game, which Quinn called sharp.
Quinn said the team dealt with injuries in the secondary and at receiver and had to ready multiple players late in the week, but did not name them.

signals.claim: Will keep using his legs when needed, without forcing runs, and manage the offense sharply
signals.note: Quinn's praise for his legs and decision-making suggests a stable dual-threat role, which supports rushing upside.

topics.detail: Quinn said the team should have clocked the ball early instead of trying to gain more yards for a kick, and that he has no timeouts-related excuses. He said the situation will be drilled more in walkthroughs, practices, and two-minute work.

Quinn said the defense allowed three straight touchdown drives after holding the opponent to about six points through most of the third quarter. He said the team has been digging in on its response and needs to close out games with a lead.
Quinn said he wants pre-snap penalties corrected and has not yet formed an assessment. He had not yet reviewed the Amik Robertson goal-line pass interference call.
